subject: Problem with multiple lines graph in ggvis compared to ggplot2

messages.author: 0581bfa66e668254
messages.subject: Problem with multiple lines graph in ggvis compared to ggplot2
parts:
I'm fairly new to the ggvis package and I'm trying to replicate some common plots I've made with ggplot2.  Right now I'm trying to replicate a line plot in which there are multiple lines for each level of a group.  For example, I'm trying to replicate a multiple line graph plotting the average length over the different dose groups for each level of supp using the ToothGrowth data set (example adapted from the Cookbook for R site and the R Graphics Cookbook):

# load data set 
data(ToothGrowth)

# load dplyr
library(dplyr)

# summarize data set to get averange length for each supp and dose combination
tg <- ToothGrowth %>%
  group_by(supp, dose) %>%
  summarize(length = mean(len, na.rm = TRUE))

# create ggplot2 version of plot
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(tg, aes(x=dose, y=length, colour=supp)) + geom_line()

# create ggvis version of plot
library(ggvis)
tg %>%
  ggvis(~dose, ~length, stroke = ~supp) %>%
  layer_lines()

The ggplot2 version correctly shows only two lines with different colors, while the ggvis version is showing three lines and with the same color for each line.  How can I properly recreate this graph with ggvis?  Please see the attached images for each version of the plot.

Thanks,
Eric.

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Problem with multiple lines graph in ggvis compared to ggplot2
parts:
Hi, I think you're running into this problem:
https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis/issues/267

It's because of a bug in dplyr, which has been fixed in the
development version. If you install the latest development versions of
ggvis and dplyr, it should work properly now. See the install
instructions here:
https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis

-Winston

Regards,
Eric
